interest: This document provides insight into pre-World War II American anxieties and surveillance regarding the Japanese diaspora and commercial fishing fleets on the Pacific Coast. Specifically, it reflects suspicions held by American patriotic and veterans' organizations that Japanese-owned commercial fishing vessels operating off California were serving as auxiliary naval craft manned by Japanese naval officers, while also demonstrating the State Department's decimal indexing and cross-referencing system connecting naval intelligence to commercial fisheries files.
overview: This file consists of a single State Department List of Papers sheet for decimal file 894.325 (Personnel. Organization. Discipline. Mutiny. Compulsory Naval Services., Japan, Auxiliary Services). It records an entry dated February 26, 1934 (OCR misread as 1954) from the Disabled Veterans of the U.S., Inc. in Long Beach, California, concerning Japanese fishing boats operating off the coast of California. The organization reported that many of the owners of these vessels were Japanese citizens and officers in the Japanese Navy, cross-referencing the underlying correspondence to file 611.C06-Fish/16.

subfiles.summary: This list of papers docket sheet indexes State Department decimal file 894.325 relating to auxiliary services of the Japanese Navy. It records a communication dated February 26 from the Disabled Veterans of the U.S., Inc. in Long Beach, California, advising that owners of Japanese fishing boats on the California coast were Japanese citizens and active or reserve naval officers. The underlying document itself was cross-referenced and filed under 611.C06-Fish/16.
